message.reasoning:
need to fix imports and class definitions. The test uses JUnit 5 annotations: @ExtendWith, @BeforeEach, @Test, @DisplayName, assertions like assertNotNull, assertThrows, assertTrue, assertEquals. Need imports: org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith, org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach, org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName, org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*. Also need MockitoExtension: org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension.

Need imports for java.io.* (InputStream, IOException, ByteArrayInputStream). java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets. Need imports for JsonSchemaFactory, JsonSchema, ValidationResult, SchemaValidatorsConfig, VersionFlag (probably com.networknt.schema.VersionFlag). Also need import for com.networknt.schema.*.

Also need to ensure the inner class ClosableFailingInputStream defined twice: one at top, another inside test method. Duplicate class name inside method shadows outer; it's okay. But outer class defined at top is fine.

But there is a comment duplication: two Javadoc comments, but not error.

Need to ensure class is public? JUnit can run with package-private. Keep as class.

Add necessary imports.

Also need to handle that JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(VersionFlag.V7) is correct method? In networknt json-schema-validator library, there is JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(SpecVersion.VersionFlag). Actually library version: com.networknt.schema.JsonSchemaFactory has method getInstance(SpecVersion.VersionFlag). The enum is com.networknt.schema.SpecVersion.VersionFlag. So need import com.networknt.schema.SpecVersion.VersionFlag; Or maybe JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(SpecVersion.VersionFlag.V7). We'll import com.networknt.schema.SpecVersion.VersionFlag.

Also need import com.networknt.schema.SchemaValidatorsConfig; import com.networknt.schema.ValidationResult; import com.networknt.schema.JsonSchema; import com.networknt.schema.JsonSchemaFactory.

Add import for java.util.* maybe not needed.

Now compile.

Potential issue: In test getSchema_validJsonWithCustomConfig_respectsConfig, they call schema.validate(instance) where instance is a JSON string but schema expects JSON object? It's okay.

Also need to import org.junit.jupiter.api.function.Executable? Not needed.

Now produce corrected code.
